value.source_text: This Section is based on the recent publication ‘Revised Section F: Natural Products and Related Compounds, IUPAC Recommendations 1999’ and the additional document ‘Corrections and Modifications 2004’ (ref. 9).
basis_documents: Revised Section F: Natural Products and Related Compounds, IUPAC Recommendations 1999

value.source_text: Many naturally occurring compounds belong to well defined structural classes, each of which can be characterized by a set of parent structures that are closely related structurally, that is, each can be derived from a fundamental parent structure by one or more defined operations used in systematic substitutive nomenclature (see P-13).
value.class_characterization: a set of closely related parent structures
value.derivation_basis: one or more defined operations used in systematic substitutive nomenclature

steps.source_text: As soon as the structure of a simple new natural product has been fully determined, the trivial name should be abandoned in favor of a systematic name formed by the Rules prescribed in Chapters P-1 through P-9 for systematic nomenclature of organic compounds.
steps.basis: Rules prescribed in Chapters P-1 through P-9

steps.source_text: For a more complicated structure, an existing semisystematic name listed in P-101.2.7 is used to fully name the compound.
If a previously known parent structure cannot be found, a new parent structure is formed and numbered as follows.
steps.condition: no previously known parent structure can be found
steps.action: form and number a new parent structure

steps.source_text: To form and number a new parent structure, the procedure described in the following subsections is followed.
steps.procedure: the procedure described in the following subsections
steps.application: formation and numbering of a new parent structure

steps.source_text: The following rules are applicable to new parent structures.

value.source_text: Existing parent structure names are considered as retained names if they do not follow the new rules (see Table 10.1).
value.condition: existing parent structure name does not follow the new rules

steps.condition: the entire stereoparent hydride is fully saturated
steps.source_text: (a) ‘ane’, if the entire stereoparent hydride is fully saturated;

steps.condition: the cyclic or the main chain of the acyclic part contains the maximum number of noncumulative double bonds
steps.source_text: (b) ‘ene’, if the cyclic or the main chain of the acyclic part contains the maximum number of noncumulative double bonds;

steps.condition: an otherwise fully saturated parent structure contains one or more individual mancude rings
steps.source_text: (c) ‘arane’, if, in an otherwise fully saturated parent structure, one or more individual mancude rings is present.

value.source_text: Existing names of parent structures in which endings are different from those indicated above, for example morphinan and ibogamine, are exceptions and treated as retained names.
value.condition: ending differs from the indicated endings

steps.action: examine the skeleton to identify the senior ring or ring system
steps.source_text: (a) examine the skeleton to identify the senior ring or ring system, according to P-44.

steps.target: the atom of the senior ring system whose locant would be 1 according to systematic numbering for that particular ring or ring system
steps.source_text: The locant ‘1’ is assigned to the atom of the senior ring system whose locant would be ‘1’ according to systematic numbering for that particular ring or ring system;

steps.action: assign all skeletal atoms of the senior ring system consecutive Arabic numbers
steps.includes: atoms of fusion positions in fused ring systems
steps.path: the path prescribed for that particular type of ring or ring system
steps.source_text: (b) assign all skeletal atoms of the senior ring system consecutive Arabic numbers, including atoms of fusion positions in fused ring systems, beginning with the locant ‘1’, and following the path prescribed for that particular type of ring or ring system;

steps.action: number acyclic substituents to skeletal atoms of ring components or connecting acyclic structures each in its entirety
steps.order_basis: increasing value of the locant of the skeletal atom to which it is attached
steps.source_text: (c) number acyclic substituents to skeletal atoms of ring components or connecting acyclic structures each in its entirety, including branches, in order of the increasing value of the locant of the skeletal atom to which it is attached;

steps.action: number skeletal atoms of acyclic connections to other ring or ring systems consecutively
steps.start: the atom next to the senior ring system
steps.then: the skeletal atoms of the other rings or ring systems as prescribed in step (b)
steps.source_text: (d) number skeletal atoms of acyclic connections to other ring or ring systems, if any, consecutively beginning with the atom next to the senior ring system, followed by the skeletal atoms of the other rings or ring systems as prescribed in (b) above;

steps.condition: two or more acyclic connections to other rings or ring systems are present
steps.order_basis: lowest numbered attachment position on the senior ring or ring system
sequence: acyclic connector at the next lower position
steps.source_text: if two or more acyclic connections to other rings or ring systems are present, the one attached to the senior ring or ring system at the lowest numbered position is numbered first, then the ring attached to it, followed by the acyclic connector at the next lower position of the senior ring or ring system, etc.;

steps.condition: two groups at a geminal disubstituted position
steps.priority: larger group in terms of number of skeletal atoms
steps.source_text: (e) number the larger group, in terms of the number of skeletal atoms, between two groups at a geminal disubstituted position first;
if there is still a choice, alphanumerical order is followed (Rule P-14.5).

steps.condition: the two groups are identical and attached to a properly drawn stereoparent structure
steps.tie_breaker: the group that is stereochemically α is numbered first
steps.source_text: If the two groups are then identical and attached to a stereoparent structure properly drawn (see Appendix 3), the group that is stereochemically ‘α’ (according to P-101.2.6) is numbered first;

steps.condition: the two groups are identical and attached to an acyclic terminal double bond
steps.tie_breaker: the group trans to the main chain is numbered first
steps.source_text: if the two groups are identical and attached to an acyclic terminal double bond, the group ‘trans’ to the main chain is numbered first, as described in the carotenoid recommendations (Rule 12.4 in ref. 40).

Since locants are used to describe skeletal modifications, as indicated in P-101.3, the identification of individual rings by letters A, B, C, etc., used in the past is no longer recommended, except for the rather special case of the removal of a terminal ring (see P-101.3.6).
steps.not_recommended: identification of individual rings by letters A, B, C, etc.

steps.source_text: Nevertheless, to provide continuity with the use of this system, names using letters to identify rings are given where appropriate, but are no longer recommended.
steps.continuity_use: names using letters to identify rings may be given where appropriate

steps.source_text: For nomenclature purposes, the fundamental parent structures are described by specific arrangements of atoms or groups of atoms called ‘atomic connectors’, ‘terminal segments’ and ‘bond connectors’, that must be taken into consideration in accordance with the additive or subtractive operations modifying a fundamental parent structure.
steps.context: additive or subtractive operations modifying a fundamental parent structure

value.source_text: An ‘atomic connector’ is a chain of homogeneous skeletal atoms of the same element connecting any combination of bridgehead or ring junction atoms, rings, or ring systems (i.e. ring assemblies), substituted skeletal atoms in parent structure, or heteroatoms.
value.composition: a chain of homogeneous skeletal atoms of the same element
connects: substituted skeletal atoms in a parent structure

value.source_text: A ‘terminal segment’ of a skeletal structure is an acyclic portion of homogeneous skeletal atoms connected at only one end by the features of structure that terminate atomic connectors.
value.composition: an acyclic portion of homogeneous skeletal atoms
value.termination: features of structure that terminate atomic connectors

value.source_text: A ‘bond connector’ is a connection between any combination of bridgehead or ring junction atoms, rings, or ring systems (i.e. ring assemblies), substituted skeletal atoms, or heteroatoms.

steps.source_text: The structures below illustrate atomic connectors, bond connectors, and terminal segments.
The use of these terms is further illustrated in P-101.3.1 in relation to the removal of skeletal atoms denoted by the prefix ‘nor’.

steps.layout: one empty data cell spans both table columns

steps.source_text: The name of a fundamental parent structure usually implies the absolute configuration of all chirality centers and the configuration of double bonds, when applicable, without further specification.
implies: absolute configuration of all chirality centers
configuration of double bonds when applicable

steps.source_text: All chirality must be defined so that for example with a steroid the stereochemistry at ‘C-5’, when relevant, is indicated by α, β or ξ. When a planar or quasi planar system of rings is denoted as a projection, as in this recommendation, an atom or group attached to the ring is called ‘α’ if it lies below or ‘β’ if it lies above the plane of the paper.

projection.alpha: attached atom or group lies below the plane of the paper
projection.beta: attached atom or group lies above the plane of the paper

steps.source_text: Use of this system requires the orientations of structure as given in the examples used to exemplify the various rules and in Appendix 3.
steps.requirement: use the orientations of structure given in the rule examples and Appendix 3
steps.basis: Appendix 3 and examples used to exemplify the various rules

steps.source_text: The stereodescriptors ‘α’, ‘β’, and ‘ξ’ used to describe implicit or indicated configuration are cited before the name of the fundamental parent structure without parentheses.
steps.position: before the name of the fundamental parent structure

steps.source_text: The ‘α/β’ symbolism is used as defined above and extended in the following way to express different aspects of the configuration of modified fundamental parent structures.
steps.purpose: express different aspects of the configuration of modified fundamental parent structures
